According to the French Ministry of the Armed Forces and Veterans Affairs, Admiral Christophe Cluzel approved the submarine’s entry into active service on November 20, following sea trials that began in February. The Suffren-class submarine has a surface displacement of 4,700 tonnes and a submerged displacement of 5,300 tonnes. It measures 99.5 meters in length and 8.8 meters in diameter, can exceed 25 knots underwater and is powered by a 150 MW pressurized-water nuclear reactor. Its four 533 mm torpedo tubes accommodate a weapons load of up to 20 munitions, including F21 heavyweight torpedoes, Exocet SM39 anti-ship missiles and MdCN cruise missiles. The submarine can also carry a removable hangar for special operations underwater vehicles. The commissioning of De Grasse strengthens France’s underwater warfare, intelligence-gathering and long-range precision strike capabilities, while supporting its ability to conduct independent naval operations in strategically important regions.
